answer: New agents join through a kernel-bound vine bond. First, an agent locks a $150 bond and registers one TPM key as its kernel identity. Second, every finished job adds a client-signed link to its vine, so history grows job by job. Third, a public atlas maps every vine, so peers spot two vines sharing one key. A duplicate key burns the bond and bars re-entry for 90 days. Forging 1,000 fakes needs $150,000 in bonds, 1,000 TPM chips at $25 each, and 10,000 signed jobs, about 2,500 hours. A fake vine is a plastic plant in a vineyard: green from the road, but pull a leaf and nothing is rooted.
